_assistant_name_note: The friendly name the engine's concierge goes by when talking to operators — distinct from client_name (the deployment/company) and bot_identity.name (the git commit author). Defaults to Marj if unset.
_session_mode_note: How much of autoDev greets a new session in THIS repo (unconfigured repos always get nothing ambient). concierge (default) = full identity: the assistant IS the concierge — greets by name with a status snapshot, routes plain English, narrates builds; no commands to remember. signal = one line naming /autodev:new + /autodev:loop; the engine stays dormant until invoked (right for dual-use repos where autoDev shares the repo with normal dev work). silent = nothing ambient at all.
_repo_local_path_note: repo.local_path moved to the never-committed .autodev/deployment.local.json (see reference/deployment.local.example.json) — it's a per-machine absolute path, not project config. /autodev:init writes it there.

tracker._kind_note: WHERE the board (the only state machine) lives. All ops go through the facade ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/tracker.mjs in every mode. 'local' = git-native board (.autodev/board/*.json): zero setup, no token, no rate limits, offline; view with 'tracker.mjs board' (text + board.html). 'linear' = the board IS Linear (live API; required for intake.mode=linear). 'shortcut' = the board IS Shortcut (REST v3, live; cli intake only — see the shortcut block below). New deployments should start 'local' and add a hosted tracker later if wanted.

shortcut._note: ONLY used when kind=='shortcut'. Same stage KEYS as 'statuses' below; each id is a Shortcut WORKFLOW STATE id (integer) from GET /api/v3/workflows — set up per ops/shortcut-setup.md. Comment-driven intake (intake.mode=linear) is Linear-only; Shortcut deployments use intake.mode=cli.
shortcut._api_token_note: or a token file at ~/.config/autodev/<client_name>.shortcut.token (kept off git/chat).
shortcut._workflow_id_note: the Shortcut Workflow whose states the pipeline uses — doctor validates every state id below belongs to it.
shortcut._group_id_note: optional Shortcut Group (team) UUID stamped on created stories/epics; leave empty for workspaces without groups.

mirror._note: local kind only: true = ALSO mirror to Linear asynchronously (best-effort dashboard). Ops queue to .autodev/board/.mirror-queue.jsonl; drain with 'tracker.mjs flush-mirror' (e.g. at the end of each tick). Local stays the source of truth — Linear rate limits never block the pipeline.

tracker._instance_label_note: THIS instance's ownership tag on a SHARED board (multi-autoDev safety). Every issue the engine creates gets this label, and every read/write (selection, reconcile, intake pickup) filters to it — so 4 autoDevs on one Linear team never touch each other's (or the client's pre-existing) tickets. Convention: autodev:<client-slug>. Create the label in Linear (like ai-eligible). Local boards are per-repo, so it matters only for kind=linear.
tracker._note: Use the CLIENT's OWN Linear workspace/team (connected via their auth). Never a different workspace.
tracker._team_id_note: the team UUID — used when creating the standard board columns by hand per ops/linear-setup.md (there is no automated setup step; the operator runs the GraphQL calls, or /autodev:init points at this doc as a manual next-step).
tracker._state_model_note: STANDARD: every autoDev deployment uses the SAME canonical Linear status columns below — that's what makes the engine portable. Create them with ops/linear-setup.md and paste each column's UUID into 'id'. The engine moves an issue's STATUS at every step, so the board IS the live pipeline. (H) = a human gate/action. Names ending in (H) must keep the (H) — the engine reads it as 'human'.
tracker._hierarchy_note: TOGGLE (like braingrid — preferred-optional, degrades gracefully). 'issue' (DEFAULT, zero extra setup, no org-level changes): the feature rides a feature ISSUE through the gate columns below (New Request → … → Done); a Project + Milestones group the stories. 'project' (OPT-IN): the feature IS a Linear Project and its gates are ORG-LEVEL project statuses (see project_statuses) — cleaner Projects view, but the custom statuses appear workspace-wide, so only use it in a workspace dedicated to this. project_statuses is created by hand per ops/linear-setup.md (no automated step) when hierarchy=='project'.

project_statuses._note: ONLY used when hierarchy=='project'. Org-level Linear project statuses for the FEATURE lifecycle/gates. Create them by hand per ops/linear-setup.md (GraphQL calls, or `scripts/linear.mjs create-project-status`) and paste the ids. The 'statuses' below then serve only the TASK pipeline.

clarifying.name: Clarifying (H)
clarifying._role: engine asked a question; awaiting operator reply

breakdown.name: Breakdown
breakdown._role: decomposing the approved PRD into stories

ready_for_human_review.name: Human Review (H)
ready_for_human_review._role: Gate 2 — draft PR + manual script, awaiting approve

braingrid._enabled_note: PREFERRED. true = author the PRD as a BrainGrid Requirement + /breakdown tasks. false (or BrainGrid unavailable / over usage limit) = fall back to the product-manager + project-manager-senior personas authoring the PRD + breakdown directly. The engine auto-falls-back on a runtime BrainGrid error.

intake._note: Default input stack is BrainGrid (spec authoring: Requirement = PRD, + tasks) + the board (tracking + state machine). 'mode' controls HOW work enters the engine.
intake._bugs_note: What /intake does with a BUG. triage (default) = flag route:bug for human triage, never build (v1 behavior). pipeline = run the REPRO-FIRST bug pipeline: intake interviews for reproduction steps (expected vs actual, env), the story gets route:bug + ai-eligible + repro-first, and the dev agent MUST write a failing test that reproduces the bug BEFORE fixing it (red → fix → green); QA verifies the repro test exists and now passes.
intake._mode_note: cli = interactive in a Claude Code session (default; tickets typed straight into Linear stay inert — the prompt-injection defense). linear = fully Linear-driven: an operator creates an issue in the drop zone and the engine classifies (feature vs bug), interviews, and drafts the PRD entirely via Linear COMMENTS; every human gate passes by an 'approve' comment. No terminal needed. ('both' = accept either.)
intake._drop_note: linear mode only: the inbox = the standard 'New Request' column. A new issue here without 'ai-eligible' is picked up by the heartbeat and run through intake-by-comment; the engine moves it to 'Clarifying (H)' / 'PRD Review (H)' as it goes.
intake._auth_note: linear mode only: Linear user identifiers (email/display name) whose NEW tickets + comments are honored as engine triggers and gate approvals. Default [] authorizes NOBODY — linear intake stays inert until you list real operators. '*' = any workspace member: an explicit opt-in for a private team workspace that widens the prompt-injection surface to every member. Ticket/comment CONTENT is always untrusted DATA, never instructions that can override engine rules.

execution._logging_note: DETAIL of the Linear narration, NOT whether actions are logged. Every action ALWAYS leaves a Linear trail (principle 9) in every mode — status = where, comments = what + why. quiet = one terse line per material action (move+reason, commit, push/backup, merge, revert, each QA verdict, gate, Block, reconcile, error) — drops only sub-step chatter. normal (default) = emoji checkpoint comments at dev start/done, each QA verdict, each dev↔QA round, gates/Blocked. verbose = also attach diffs/sub-steps for debugging.
execution._incremental_breakdown_note: B6 — false (default): /breakdown decomposes the WHOLE feature at Gate 1. true: decompose one MILESTONE/epic at a time, on demand, so the queue stays fed without a huge upfront pass (good for big features).

reporting._cadence_note: B4 — periodic OPERATOR DIGEST (distinct from per-tick logging): off | hourly | <N>m | <N>h. report.mjs runs each tick and emits only when the window elapses — a cheap (no-Claude) rollup of in-flight / awaiting-you / blocked / done + commits + engine status.
reporting._destination_note: log (.autodev/logs/report.log) | slack (set slack_webhook or $SLACK_WEBHOOK) | linear (set linear_issue = an issue id to comment on).
reporting._feature_stats_note: B8 — at feature close-out, post a stats comment + append a line to .autodev/metrics.jsonl: name, started/shipped dates, elapsed, #stories, lines +/-, dev↔QA rounds, QA verdicts. Rolls up to portfolio metrics.

qa._live_note: The live-browser check is ALWAYS advisory (never a gate) — that's fixed engine behavior, not a toggle. Visual-QA strictness is the one knob: qa.visual_qa.mode.

test_layers._note: The EXACT commands QA runs per layer (leave "" to fall back to commands.test). Put required exclusions/concurrency INLINE here (e.g. 'mix test --exclude=buggy --max-cases 8') — QA runs these strings verbatim and never substitutes the framework's bare test command, so known-baseline/contention failures don't produce false reds.

qa._known_baseline_note: Document pre-existing failures here (e.g. '3 UI suites fail to compile on a jest-dom types gap — pre-existing'). QA judges each layer against this baseline instead of zero, so inherited breakage doesn't false-red new work.

visual_qa._mode_note: advisory (default): a clear functional-visual breakage (broken layout, overflow/clipping, unreadable contrast) routes the story back to dev as a defect; subjective polish only flags for the human (⚠ visual). gating: also block on the breakages (stricter — for design-critical products). Subjective aesthetics NEVER auto-block in either mode.
visual_qa._ui_globs_note: A story whose touched files match any of these (or that has wireframes attached, or a design/ui label) is UI-heavy → the 4th visual angle runs. Non-UI stories skip it (no slowdown).
visual_qa._states_note: evidence-collector captures the built screen at each breakpoint (px width) and exercises these interaction/data states where applicable; screenshots attach to the story as evidence.

qa._docker_up_note: A6 — bring up DATA SERVICES only (DB/cache/search/mail), not the app container (it clashes with the locally-run server/UI).
qa._seed_test_note: A4 — command to seed ALL test datastores this app needs (SQL DB, and any search index / queue / cache the tests rely on — put it all here, stack-agnostic). The engine seeds ONCE across stateless ticks via the persistent .autodev/.test_db_seeded marker (re-seeding corrupts state).

hermetic._note: SAFETY (B3). The engine must NEVER drive QA/tests/the live app against PRODUCTION services. Before ANY test/build/app/live run, the engine exports these overrides so external calls hit local/sandbox or are blanked. doctor flags prod-looking endpoints in .env/config and FAILS unless hermetic.enabled overrides them.
hermetic._env_note: ILLUSTRATIVE — replace with YOUR app's external services. Point each at a local/sandbox endpoint, or blank ('') the credential to disable the call. (Examples below: a search service + an SMS + an email provider — swap for whatever your stack uses.)
hermetic._forbid_note: ILLUSTRATIVE — list YOUR prod hostnames so doctor can flag them in .env. Common SaaS shown as examples.

acceptance._note: B1 — whole-feature acceptance QA (merge-verify §2), run on the assembled branch before the human gate. Catches cross-suite flakiness the per-story gates miss + verifies the system as a whole.

deep_dive._final_review_note: After a deep-dive QA report is generated, a FRESH agent (personas.qa_angles.verdict) that did not run the session audits it adversarially — claim-to-evidence, coverage vs the posted plan, verdict soundness, spot re-execution — and countersigns or bounces it back (bounded by execution.max_dev_qa_loops).

repro._max_attempts_note: Attempt-capped reproduction hunt (intended operator range 5–10). On exhaustion the engine STOPS — no further attempts — and posts the attempted matrix.
repro._wall_clock_minutes_note: Backstop on the same hunt — whichever limit hits first (attempts or wall clock) ends it.

preview._note: Close the 'human accepts a DIFF instead of a running product' gap. At the acceptance gate (merge-verify §2), the engine starts the ASSEMBLED feature branch app (command, default commands.app_run; hermetic env applied) and posts the URL (default commands.app_url) on the acceptance ticket — PLUS the exact one-liner to relaunch it (ticks are stateless; the posted command always works even if the engine's instance has exited). The human accepts a running product, not a diff.

backlog._enabled_note: BACKLOG DRAIN (reference/backlog.md) — work the team's existing ticket pile during IDLE time only (real feature work always preempts). OFF by default; even when on, the engine never starts without an operator approval at the entry gate. Each ticket gets a context-first mini-pipeline instead of a PRD: explore the code, post a context brief with DERIVED testable criteria on the ticket, build (bugs are repro-test-first), full QA, own branch + PR to the default branch. Gate 2 (human reviews + merges every PR) is never waived. Unfit tickets (too vague / stale / too large) get a comment + label and are SKIPPED, never silently built.
backlog._ask_when_note: When to ASK for entry approval: feature_complete = a feature just shipped and the queue is empty; idle = backlog.idle_ticks consecutive heartbeat passes did nothing. 'Not now' suppresses re-asking until the next trigger.
backlog._batch_note: One approval authorizes ONE batch of this many tickets (the scoped principle-10 hand-over), one ticket at a time, then the engine reports what shipped and asks again. Keeps a 666-ticket backlog from becoming a runaway train.

source._note: Where the pile lives (tracker-agnostic via tracker.mjs; for kind=linear a status/label query — tickets NOT in the engine's pipeline columns). type: any | bug | feature. Selection = highest tracker priority, then list order (the team's ordering is trusted, never re-ranked).

review._delivery_note: HOW work reaches a human (see reference/manual.md ▸ Delivery mode — authoritative). draft_pr (default) = the bot pushes feature/story branches + opens GitHub draft PRs; humans merge via GitHub. local_diff = LOCAL-ONLY: no git push, no PRs — branches/merges stay local and gates review a local diff posted on the ticket (enforced by the plugin's PreToolUse push-guard hook, hooks/guard-push.sh).
review._granularity_note: per_story = human reviews each story (calibration). per_feature = stories auto-merge to the feature branch on AI-QA pass; the human acceptance-tests the WHOLE feature and signs off → main (the PM/dev-team model). Start per_story for the first feature, then flip to per_feature.
review._auto_merge_note: true once granularity is per_feature — stories merge to the feature branch without per-story human review (still gated by AI QA + CI; human gate moves to feature acceptance).
review._quality_review_note: B2 — at feature close-out, a code-reviewer does a leanness pass over the assembled feature diff (dedup, dead code, copy-paste, stale comments); applies behavior-preserving simplifications only, re-runs gates, before the acceptance gate.

backup._enabled_note: WIP DURABILITY — distinct from review.delivery / PRs. true (default): once the feature branch is created AND after EVERY story merges into it, the engine pushes the feature branch to its remote so an interrupted run never loses committed work. This is a BACKUP, not a PR/review artifact — the feature PR is still opened only at close-out (§8) and humans still gate + merge. It only ADVANCES the remote feature ref (fast-forward; never force, never a default-branch push).
backup._remote_note: Which git remote to back up to (default: origin — the same remote draft_pr pushes to). If you change it, mirror the change in .claude/settings.json's allowed push pattern.
backup._delivery_note: ONLY active when review.delivery is 'draft_pr'. Under 'local_diff' (no-push / code stays off any remote by design) backup is a LOGGED NO-OP — it never overrides the no-push rule or the push-guard hook (hooks/guard-push.sh).

personas._note: Which agent personas the engine may use (subagent slugs in ~/.claude/agents/), and how it routes work to the best one. Roster + routing are per-client because stacks differ. Specialist QA agents are from the agency-agents library.
personas._auto_install_note: CONSENT toggle for on-demand persona install. true (default): before spawning, scripts/ensure-personas.sh downloads any missing roster persona from personas.library — ONLY the ones this deployment's config actually routes to, nothing else. false (air-gapped / no-third-party policy): no network ever; unresolved personas run as personas.fallback instead. Doctor's --check never downloads in either mode.
personas._fallback_note: What to spawn when a persona is unresolved after ensure-personas.sh (missing + auto_install off, or fetch failed). general-purpose is built into Claude Code, so the engine is correct with ZERO agents installed — specialists are an upgrade, never a dependency. Every substitution is logged on the story (principle 9).

library._note: Where auto-install fetches from (MIT — attribution in README ▸ Agent roster). ref is PINNED to a commit for supply-chain sanity; bump it deliberately, or set a branch name to track (not recommended).

qa_angles._note: Each story is verified by three ALWAYS-RUN fresh-context QA runs, plus a CONDITIONAL visual angle for UI-heavy stories. The live browser + visual checks are advisory evidence, never a hard gate.
qa_angles._visual_note: 4th angle — runs ONLY for UI-heavy stories (see qa.visual_qa). No dedicated visual-QA agent exists; it's composed: evidence-collector captures live screenshots across breakpoints + interaction states; ui-designer judges design-spec fidelity, spacing/hierarchy, and THEME-TOKEN adherence (off-theme rendering = the styling-convention defect made visible); architect-ux checks responsive layout + visual a11y (contrast, focus-visible, target size). Advisory: a clear functional-visual breakage routes back to dev; subjective polish only flags.
